author: Dr. Meena Rao (Linguist A)
note: The kinship term 'dada' placed sentence-final (as in E04 'dada ni firli mo?') signals a still-tense or unresolved relationship. When placed sentence-initial with 'firli' (as in E07, post-reconciliation), it signals warmth and resolution. This is a RELATIONSHIP-STATE marker, not free variation.

author: Prof. K. Iyer (Linguist B)
note: I disagree partially with Dr. Rao. I believe the word-order shift in E04 vs E07 is about VERB CHOICE ('aau' vs 'firli'), not the position of 'dada'. 'firli' specifically implies 'returning home/to the fold' and is what carries the reconciliation meaning, independent of word order.

author: S. Dutta (Field Consultant)
note: Both of the above are plausible. Recommend flagging any subtitle involving 'dada' + a return/coming verb for human review until we get more paired examples across relationship states.
